ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Neurologic event at higher exposure

A 44-year-old man treated with clozapine has a generalized seizure after rapid dose escalation. Glucose and sodium are normal, and there is no acute intracranial lesion. Which property of clozapine is most relevant to this event?

  1. Direct correction of metabolic seizure triggers
  2. Dose-related lowering of the seizure threshold
  3. Reliable anticonvulsant activity at higher doses
  4. Selective neuromuscular junction blockade
  5. Universal seizure risk limited to the first dose
Answer and explanation

Dose-related lowering of the seizure threshold

Clozapine seizure risk is related to exposure, supporting cautious titration and review of contributors.

Option explanations

Dose-related lowering of the seizure threshold: Clozapine seizure risk is related to exposure, supporting cautious titration and review of contributors.

Reliable anticonvulsant activity at higher doses: Clozapine does not provide this protective effect.

Selective neuromuscular junction blockade: This would cause weakness rather than a generalized cortical seizure.

Universal seizure risk limited to the first dose: Risk is not confined to the first administration.

Direct correction of metabolic seizure triggers: The drug does not prevent seizures through normalization of electrolytes.
